speaker: Eliezer Yudkowsky
event: TED2023 talk 'Will superintelligent AI end the world?' (TED). Full upload on the TED YouTube channel (video Yd0yQ9yxSYY, 632.6 s). The talk body ends at about 343 s ('Thank you for coming to my brief TED talk'); a host Q&A runs from about 355 s to the end of the upload.
date_note: The TED talk page lists the talk as TED2023 and dated April 2023. The exact day was not confirmed from the sources reached here. A TED Talks Daily podcast listing dated 2023-07-11 is a podcast release date, not the talk date.

lines.verbatim: We do not get to learn from our mistakes and try again because everyone is already dead.
lines.notes: Strongest match for the 'no second try' and 'everyone dying' beats in one line. Mid-talk, inside the talk body. The small.en pass adds a comma after 'again'; the wording is identical in both passes.

lines.verbatim: If we actually try to do this in real life, we are all going to die.
lines.notes: Direct 'we are all going to die' line, mid-talk. Wording identical in base.en and small.en passes; punctuation is Whisper's.

lines.verbatim: I say this, expecting that we all just die.
lines.notes: Near the end of the talk body. Preceded by 'I say this, not expecting that to actually happen.' The lead-in gives context for the line. Wording identical in both passes; the small.en clip check drops the comma only.

verification.method: Audio only. The official TED transcript page was not fetched, and no third-party transcript was used as the source of the wording.
